neighbours.label: amusement and play: fun games, jokes, silly twists and laughter
fire: At the sleepover the girls made up a silly version of tag played in the dark.
The clown kept the whole crowd giggling with his squeaky balloon tricks.
We spent the rainy afternoon playing board games and cracking jokes.
Our coach turned warm-ups into a goofy relay with rubber chickens.
The comedian had the audience roaring with laughter for an hour.
Grandma loves playing peekaboo with the baby until he squeals with delight.
At the carnival we tried the ring toss, the funhouse and the bumper cars.
The cousins pulled harmless pranks on each other all summer for fun.
quiet: At the sleepover the girls made a careful list of chores for the morning.
The clerk kept the whole line waiting while he checked each receipt.
We spent the rainy afternoon filing paperwork and paying overdue bills.
Our coach turned warm-ups into a strict routine of measured sprints.
The lecturer had the audience taking notes on tax law for an hour.
Grandma checks the baby's temperature twice a day while he has a fever.
At the county office we renewed the permit, paid the fee and signed forms.
The cousins repaired the fence on each other's farms all summer for pay.
